metadata.explanation: Chains highlight removal with strikethrough on the last sentence 'It was nice speaking with you, and we will be in touch.' Evaluator checks (1) no char highlights (0.5 pts) and (2) the last sentence's paragraph/span style has style:text-line-through-style set to a non-none value (0.5 pts). Initial state fails both: highlights exist, no strikethrough. [Fixed: renamed function suffix from 16-char '66b3d4ffc50e39d9' to correct 32-char MD5 'a30ceeb68a8eeb0b8a512ab61a2387e1'; moved private helper functions inside main getter as nested functions to satisfy get_ naming rule; Fix 3: removed all nested def statements by inlining helper logic directly in the main getter body, eliminating load_odt/has_char_highlights/get_style_text_props/collect_para_style_names defs that the validator flagged]
metadata.task_rationale: Hardened variation combining highlight removal with selective strikethrough on the document's closing sentence. Tests targeted text selection and formatting.

scoring_breakdown.last_sentence_strikethrough: 0.5 - Last sentence 'It was nice speaking...' has strikethrough

llm_judge_reasons: Both instruction requirements are covered: 'no_highlights' (0.5 pts) and 'last_sentence_strikethrough' (0.5 pts) are each verified by the evaluator.
Getter correctly reads ODT file from the VM, parses content.xml and styles.xml, and checks character-family styles for fo:background-color to detect highlights — the correct approach for ODT format.

Getter correctly searches for the last-sentence paragraph using a substring match ('It was nice speaking with you'), collects relevant style names, and checks text-line-through-style attribute in those styles — the correct ODF attribute for strikethrough.
Metric function correctly handles the expected parameter for type='rule': it does not misuse expected.get('rules') and instead directly reads result keys, awarding partial credit correctly.
Postconfig saves the file (Ctrl+S) before evaluation, ensuring file state is current when the getter reads it.

Minor: Span collection condition 'len(span_text) > 5' is overly broad — collects styles from any span with >5 chars in the paragraph, not just spans containing the last sentence. This could cause false positives in strikethrough detection if other spans in the same paragraph happen to have strikethrough for unrelated reasons.
Minor: The 'expected' parameter is entirely unused in the metric function; logic is hardcoded. Not harmful but reduces flexibility.
Minor: White (#ffffff) backgrounds would be incorrectly counted as highlights, though LibreOffice typically uses 'transparent'/'automatic' when removing highlights via 'No Fill'.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Tighten the span collection condition: replace 'last_sentence in span_text or len(span_text) > 5' with 'last_sentence in span_text' to avoid collecting unrelated span styles in the same paragraph.
Optionally exclude '#ffffff' from the highlights check (or add it to the exclusion list) to avoid false positives from white backgrounds.
Consider using the 'expected' dict (no_highlights, last_sentence_strikethrough) to drive the checks for added flexibility, though current hardcoded logic is functionally correct.

fix_history: Fix 1: Renamed function suffix from invalid 16-char '66b3d4ffc50e39d9' to correct 32-char MD5 'a30ceeb68a8eeb0b8a512ab61a2387e1' (computed from '6a33f9b9-0a56-4844-9c3f-96ec3ffb3ba2|3')

Fix 2: Moved private helper functions (_load_odt, _has_char_highlights, _get_style_text_props, _collect_para_style_names) inside the main getter as nested functions so all module-level functions satisfy the get_ naming requirement

Fix 3: Removed all nested def statements (load_odt, has_char_highlights, get_style_text_props, collect_para_style_names) by inlining their logic directly in the main getter body. The validator scans all def statements in the getter file regardless of nesting, so nested defs that violate naming rules still trigger errors. Inlining eliminates these spurious violations.
